dedupe_keys.name: forefire wildland fire spread simulation engine

description: ForeFire is an open-source engine for simulating how wildland fires spread across a landscape. Its C++ core propagates the fire front with a choice of rate-of-spread models over terrain and fuel maps stored as NetCDF, and it can be coupled two ways with an atmospheric model such as MesoNH, so that fire heat changes the wind that drives the fire. It runs through a scripting interpreter, Python bindings or Docker, and uses MPI for parallel runs. The provider is the French CNRS at the Université de Corse Pascal Paoli, where the engine is used for research and operational forecasting. Coverage is any region with fuel, terrain and weather inputs. The code is on GitHub under the GNU GPL version 3, is described in the Journal of Open Source Software, has online documentation and a live demo, and the latest tag read today is v2.5.0. Caveats: accuracy depends on fuel maps and wind forecasts, coupled runs need high-performance computing, and the engine models fire behaviour, not firefighting. Simulation uses: forecasting the fire front that emergency services must respond to, timing evacuation triggers for communities and facilities, and generating hazard footprints for infrastructure exposure. Related records: SimFire (model-simfire) is a lighter Python fire simulator, and Wildfire Risk to Communities (data-wildfire-risk-to-communities) maps community exposure in the United States.
